claim: agentgateway can front both an external managed 'strong' provider (Azure OpenAI, declared as an ai:{provider:{azure:{...}}} backend) and a self-hosted 'weak' pool (a service backend carrying a backend-level inferenceRouting policy that calls the Gateway API Inference Extension's Endpoint Picker over ext-proc), letting it act as the single gateway that decides which backend class serves a request while delegating intra-pool picking to the EPP.
stance_target: the layered pattern: gateway chooses between external and self-hosted backend classes, EPP chooses within the self-hosted pool
scope_conditions: agentgateway v1.3.1, Gateway API Inference Extension v1.0.0, AKS, validated mid-2026
quoted_support:
backends:
-service:
name: llm/workspace-phi-4-mini.llm.svc.cluster.local
port:5000
policies:
inferenceRouting:
endpointPicker:{host: phi-epp-epp.llm.svc.cluster.local:9002}
destinationMode: passthrough

claim: Because agentgateway speaks ext-proc natively and can call the Endpoint Picker directly, a deployment can drop the Gateway API Gateway object entirely and run a single data-plane (agentgateway) instead of two proxies.
stance_target: a non-Gateway-API-native AI gateway can still integrate with the EPP contract directly, without a k8s Gateway resource in front of it
quoted_support: because it speaks ext-proc itself -- call the Endpoint Picker directly so the weak path gets GPU-state placement. That third job is what lets us drop the Gateway API gateway entirely: one data plane instead of two

claim: There is no managed-cloud equivalent for the ext-proc call to the Endpoint Picker; whichever gateway fronts a self-hosted GPU pool, the operator must still run and wire that piece themselves.
stance_target: the EPP/ext-proc integration is an irreducible self-operated component even when other gateway functions are outsourced to a managed service
quoted_support: The ext-proc call to the Endpoint Picker, which places each weak-path request on the right GPU pod, has no managed equivalent today, so that piece stays yours to run whichever gateway fronts it.

claim: RouteLLM's matrix-factorization (mf) router reaches approximately 95% of GPT-4's quality on MT-Bench while making only about 26% of the GPT-4 calls, cutting cost by up to approximately 85% versus routing everything to GPT-4.
stance_target: quantitative case for a semantic-routing layer above the gateway/EPP layers
scope_conditions: RouteLLM paper's original strong/weak model pair, not validated against arbitrary pairs
quoted_support: the featured mf (matrix-factorization) router reaches ~95% of GPT-4's quality on MT-Bench while making just ~26% of the GPT-4 calls -- cutting cost by up to ~85% versus sending everything to GPT-4

claim: InferencePool and InferenceObjective are governed by different Kubernetes API groups (inference.networking.k8s.io vs inference.networking.x-k8s.io) and InferenceObjective replaces the older InferenceModel object, dropping its criticality enum in favor of a plain integer priority while taking the served-model name from the request itself.
stance_target: API evolution of the Gateway API Inference Extension CRDs, relevant to dating any API-shape claim
scope_conditions: Gateway API Inference Extension v1.0.0, mid-2026
quoted_support: It replaces the older InferenceModel object: where InferenceModel carried a modelName and a criticality enum, InferenceObjective keeps only an integer priority and takes the served-model name from the request instead.
